tagline: Complex AI. Explained visually. Built practically.
title: How Large Language Models Work
disclosure: Fictional teaching scenario. Wouri Express and its people are invented; the setting draws on documented conditions in Douala, Cameroon.

onScreen.text: Ndedi asked the chatbot about last month's delays.
onScreen.emphasis: It answered with confidence. It had never seen last month.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Ndedi pasted this week's driver messages into a chatbot and got a good summary. Then she asked about last month.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: It answered with confidence. It had never seen last month. Here is how a language model actually works.

onScreen.title: How Large Language Models Work
onScreen.subtitle: AI Fundamentals · Lesson 4 · Tokens, training and context at Wouri Express, Douala

messages.text: Ndedi: Here are this week's driver messages. Summarise the delays.
Port gate queues on Tuesday and Thursday mornings, flooding at Bonabéri, three absent customers.
Ndedi: And how did last month compare?
Last month was better, with fewer port delays and no flooding.

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: The first answer was right, Tanyi. She pasted the messages. The second answer sounds just as sure, and she pasted nothing.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: The model can only work with what is in front of it. Let me show you what it does.

scenes.label: Understand: what happens when you ask

onScreen.title: From your words to its answer

nodes.label: Context
nodes.sub: what it can see right now

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: First, tokens. Your text is cut into pieces: words, parts of words, punctuation. The model works on those pieces.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Second, training. The model read billions of words and learned which tokens tend to follow which. Then training stopped.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Third, prediction. It writes its answer one token at a time, each one the most likely next piece given everything before it.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Fourth, context: your message, what you pasted, and the conversation so far. That is all it can see.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Knowledge lives in two places. Training: general, frozen, from the past. Context: specific, now, whatever you put in front of it.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Last month's messages were in neither. So the model did what it always does: predicted a fluent answer anyway.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: And one more thing lives in context: whatever you paste. Customer phone numbers do not go into a public chatbot.

onScreen.title: Kito builds the context on purpose

steps.title: Put the facts in front of it

ui.title: Context sent to the model
lines: Instruction: summarise delays by cause, cite message numbers
Week 36: 150 driver messages, phone numbers removed

steps.title: Too much for one window
steps.detail: The context has a size limit

items.text: Does not fit in one context window
Plan: summarise each week, then summarise the summaries

messages.text: Port delays rose from 6 to 11. Flooding appears only in week 36. Sources: week 32 summary; messages 12, 15, 27, 40.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: I decide what goes in the context: the instruction, this week's messages without phone numbers, and the archived week thirty-two summary.

lines.speaker: amara
lines.text: Why not paste all three months? The context has a limit, does it not?

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: It does. So I summarise each week first, then compare summaries. Now the comparison is grounded, with sources.

messages.text: Last month was better, with fewer port delays and no flooding.
I have no messages from last month in front of me. Give me the archive and I will compare.

ui.title: Remember
lines: The model always predicts a next token
It has no built-in sense of “I was not told”
Unless you instruct it to check its context

lines.speaker: hallucinator
lines.text: Last month? Better, obviously. Fewer port delays, no flooding at all. I remember it clearly.

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: You remember nothing. There is no last month in the context. My rule: if it is not in front of me, I say so and ask for it.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: A language model always produces the next token. It has no built-in feeling of I was not told. You build that check in.

messages.text: Ndedi: Compare this week with last month.
Loaded weeks 32 to 35 from the archive. Port delays: up from an average of 7 to 11. Sources attached.

ui.title: Send messages to the model with phone numbers removed?
summary: Company account, not a public chatbot

lines.speaker: kito
lines.text: Ndedi asks the same question. This time the archive loads into the context first, and the comparison comes with sources.

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: And the messages go through the company's account, phone numbers stripped. Context is where your data goes. Guard it.

onScreen.title: Build the context, get the answer

items.label: Law office
items.text: Paste the contract, then ask about the clause

items.label: School
items.text: Give the syllabus before asking for a quiz

items.label: Shop
items.text: Attach the price list before drafting the offer

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Same rule anywhere: paste the contract before asking about the clause, the syllabus before the quiz, the price list before the offer.

onScreen.title: Who owns this?
items: The context is built by Wouri Express code, not by hand
Phone numbers and customer names are stripped first
Archives stay on the company's own storage

lines.speaker: gatekeeper
lines.text: The company's own code builds the context. Names and numbers are stripped first. Archives stay on company storage. Whoever sends data is accountable.

lines.speaker: tanyi
lines.text: Tokens, training, prediction, context. The model knows language. You supply the facts. Everything it does not have, it will guess.

lines.text: Your challenge: ask a chatbot something only you know, and watch it guess. Then paste the facts and ask again.
